result: When I moved from Phoenix to Seattle at 34, I figured the hardest part would be the rain. It turns out the hardest part was admitting I couldn't swim. In Arizona, pools were something you floated near with a drink, not something you needed to understand. In Seattle, surrounded by lakes, sound, and people who kayak on weekends, I felt that gap every time someone invited me out on the water. So I signed up for adult lessons, standing in the shallow end among a handful of equally nervous beginners. The first few sessions were humbling. I practiced blowing bubbles, kicking while holding a foam board, and trusting that my body would actually float. By lesson six, I could glide a few strokes before panicking. Lesson nine, I finally figured out breathing. And on lesson eleven, I pushed off the wall, kept my face in the water, and swam one full length of the pool without stopping. I grabbed the edge, gasping and grinning like I'd won a medal. It wasn't pretty, but it was mine. Next up: the lake, once it warms up.
